newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady on lack of offers.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady on lack of offers.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Friday after falls earlier in the week, supported by lack of lenders in the market, dealers said.
"There are few bids in the market but no offers. Lenders are apparently holding back," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

But rates could come under pressure again following maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Friday which will improve liquidity further, dealers said. A 420 million ringgit long-term government bond issue had matured on Wednesday.
"But at current levels, further falls are likely to be limited," said another local bank dealer.
Dealers said Bank Negara, to maintain a tight monetary policy, could intervene in the interbank market if rates fell sharply.
One-week and two-week money were at 6.5/7.0 percent and three-week at 7.10/20 percent, all unchanged from Wednesday.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent against 7.20/25, three-month at 7.30/35 percent from 7.25/30 and six-month at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35.
The market was closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
The overnight interbank rate is expected to fall back on Friday following the Bank Negara bills issue maturity, dealers said. "It should trade at 6.0 to 6.5 percent," a dealer said.
The overnight rate shot up to 8.7 percent on Wednesday due to borrowing by big banks in late trading.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were marginally lower.
The benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down one point at 92.67, or an implied yield of 7.33 percent.
September and December were also down one point at 92.67 and 92.66, or 7.33 and 7.34 percent respectively.
